answer: Registration binds each agent identity to a hardware-sealed credential and a 400-unit stake escrowed across 10 epochs, recorded once in the voyage registry. A sybil attacker locks 400 units per identity and forfeits 100 percent of it if independent jurors detect a duplicate credential. Copying the credential therefore costs 400 units per fake identity while the shared slash penalty propagates across every copy, leaving no knoll of unpunished duplicates and no cheap ripple of new identities.
